schema.description:
One proposed Knowledge change: the action and its fields, flat in one object. It is staged as a proposal; nothing is written until it is accepted.

Citations (in `citations`, or each section's `citations`) are resolved on the server within the caller's reach and accepted only when they name (a) the caller's own conversation: `{source_type: conversation | agent_note | user_note, source_title, meta: {excerpt}}`; (b) a file the caller uploaded, at a place the file has (a page, paragraph or line past its end is refused with the file's extent); or (c) a source Knowledge already cites on a page the caller can read. Name the source by `source_ref` (from a read), `key` (its `{{token}}`), or `reference` (the readable reference a read printed: `memo.pdf › p. 7`, `#deals › message 2026-03-04 14:02 UTC`, `OPS-12`). `{{tokens}}` in the prose are held to the same rule. Anything else is refused with `outcome.error_code` `citation_not_citeable` (or `citation_needs_excerpt`), never stored as an unrecognised source.

merge_sections.description: For merge: the ORDERED section list the surviving page should lead with, drawn from both pages -- e.g. ["canonical:sec_overview", "duplicate:sec_findings"]. Duplicate-sourced sections are moved across whole (prose, citations, dates and embeddings intact) before the duplicate is archived; canonical-sourced ones are only reordered. Sections you do not name are safe: an unnamed canonical section keeps its place after the listed ones, and an unnamed duplicate section is archived with its page. new_section_body.description: THE ENTIRE NEW BODY of the section (for edit_section). A section runs from its <!-- sec:ID --> marker to the NEXT marker, so it includes every ## and ### heading under it. Whatever you send REPLACES ALL OF IT: subsections you do not retype are DELETED, not merged, and their citations and dates go with them. Read the section first and send back everything you are keeping. To split an over-long section, create the new sections FIRST (a new section_id plus section_title, and after=<this section id>) and move the prose into them, THEN shrink this one. Include all inline citation tokens; the <!-- sec:ID --> marker is prepended automatically if omitted. The section's OWN heading is not part of the body -- it is kept as it is, or set with section_title -- so you do not need to retype it.
